positive_case: Map information without inferring process compliance.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Inferring a complete process or certification from stored content.

positive_case: Two entries and two scenarios can concern one case without identity collapse.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Merging cases solely because labels or scores match.

positive_case: Retrieve a superseded issued version without overwriting it.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Historical retrieval silently reads current mutable values.

positive_case: Equal scores on incompatible versions remain distinguishable.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Treating missing context as zero or equal values as comparability.

positive_case: Retain an unverified reported score; reject a claimed computation with missing required inputs.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Presenting supplied arithmetic as a verified calculation.

positive_case: A proposed mapping preserves its source assertion and does not create an occurrence.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Overwriting evidence or treating a correction as independent corroboration.

positive_case: Retain an assignment record without fabricating an actor or actual mandate.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Inferring Risk Owner or a second actor from documentation alone.

positive_case: A closed entry does not establish cessation; an absent rule stays unknown.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Inferring treatment effectiveness or cessation from a state label.

positive_case: The typed projection excludes untyped boundary notions and preserves bearer dependence.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Treating a description as an actual vulnerability or an untyped boundary as a typed core class.

positive_case: A scale-only threshold can be represented without inventing an indicator.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Collapsing different source meanings or inventing required evidence.

positive_case: An incomplete record remains available without a false readiness declaration.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Confusing data completeness, mapping allocation and semantic adequacy.

positive_case: Every published result identifies its input version and scope.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Inheriting a result from a different version or treating counts as semantic validity.

positive_case: Two distinct entries can refer to one case.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Entries become the case or are grouped by equal labels.

positive_case: Distinct scenario specifications link to the case.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Scenario identity is collapsed into case identity.

positive_case: Both values and their different pinned scales remain retrievable.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Numeric equality alone authorizes comparison.

positive_case: The assignment is retained without an asserted real mandate.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: A relator or second actor is invented.

positive_case: Closure and cessation evidence are independent.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Closure automatically establishes cessation.

positive_case: Its source identity, locator and interpretation origin are recoverable.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: Missing or misjoined provenance is presented as source support.

positive_case: A correction is linked to its corrected statement.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: The correction is counted as independent corroboration.

positive_case: A candidate scenario can remain incomplete without a fabricated case.
negative_or_nonentailment_case: An identity is invented to satisfy a managed-record constraint.
